urls.https://openai.com/index/language-model-: We describe our latest thinking in the hope of helping other AI developers address safety and misuse of deployed models.
urls.https://openai.com/index/formal-math: We built a neural theorem prover for Lean that learned to solve a variety of challenging high-school olympiad problems, including problems from the AMC12 and AIME competitions, as well as two problems adapted from the IMO.
urls.https://openai.com/index/instruction-fol: We’ve trained language models that are much better at following user intentions than GPT-3 while also making them more truthful and less toxic, using techniques developed through our alignment research. These InstructGPT models, which are trained with humans in the loop, are now deployed as the default language models on our API.
urls.https://openai.com/index/introducing-tex: We are introducing embeddings, a new endpoint in the OpenAI API that makes it easy to perform natural language and code tasks like semantic search, clustering, topic modeling, and classification.
urls.https://openai.com/index/webgpt: We’ve fine-tuned GPT-3 to more accurately answer open-ended questions using a text-based web browser.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-residenc: As part of our effort to support and develop AI talent, we’re excited to announce the OpenAI Residency.
urls.https://openai.com/index/api-no-waitlist: Wider availability made possible by safety progress.
urls.https://openai.com/index/solving-math-wo: We’ve trained a system that solves grade school math problems with nearly twice the accuracy of a fine-tuned GPT-3 model. It solves about 90% as many problems as real kids: a small sample of 9-12 year olds scored 60% on a test from our dataset, while our system scored 55% on those same problems.
urls.https://openai.com/index/summarizing-boo: Scaling human oversight of AI systems for tasks that are difficult to evaluate.
urls.https://openai.com/index/helen-toner-joi: Today, we’re excited to announce the appointment of Helen Toner to our board of directors.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-codex: We’ve created an improved version of OpenAI Codex, our AI system that translates natural language to code, and we are releasing it through our API in private beta starting today.
urls.https://openai.com/index/triton: We’re releasing Triton 1.0, an open-source Python-like programming language which enables researchers with no CUDA experience to write highly efficient GPU code—most of the time on par with what an expert would be able to produce.
urls.https://openai.com/index/improving-langu: Our latest research finds we can improve language model behavior with respect to specific behavioral values by fine-tuning on a small, curated dataset.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: We’re proud to announce that the 2021 class of OpenAI Scholars has completed our six-month mentorship program and have produced an open-source research project with stipends and support from OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/will-hurd-joins: OpenAI is committed to developing general-purpose artificial intelligence that benefits all humanity, and we believe that achieving our goal requires expertise in public policy as well as technology. So, we’re delighted to announce that Congressman Will Hurd has joined our board of directors.
urls.https://openai.com/index/gpt-3-apps: Over 300 applications are delivering GPT-3–powered search, conversation, text completion, and other advanced AI features through our API.
urls.https://openai.com/index/multimodal-neur: We’ve discovered neurons in CLIP that respond to the same concept whether presented literally, symbolically, or conceptually. This may explain CLIP’s accuracy in classifying surprising visual renditions of concepts, and is also an important step toward understanding the associations and biases that CLIP and similar models learn.
urls.https://openai.com/index/scaling-kuberne: We’ve scaled Kubernetes clusters to 7,500 nodes, producing a scalable infrastructure for large models like GPT-3, CLIP, and DALL·E, but also for rapid small-scale iterative research such as Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models.
urls.https://openai.com/index/dall-e: We’ve trained a neural network called DALL·E that creates images from text captions for a wide range of concepts expressible in natural language.
urls.https://openai.com/index/clip: We’re introducing a neural network called CLIP which efficiently learns visual concepts from natural language supervision. CLIP can be applied to any visual classification benchmark by simply providing the names of the visual categories to be recognized, similar to the “zero-shot” capabilities of GPT-2 and GPT-3.
urls.https://openai.com/index/organizational-: It’s been a year of dramatic change and growth at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-licenses: OpenAI has agreed to license GPT-3 to Microsoft for their own products and services.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-to-sum: We’ve applied reinforcement learning from human feedback to train language models that are better at summarization.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: Our third class of OpenAI Scholars presented their final projects at virtual Demo Day, showcasing their research results from over the past five months.
urls.https://openai.com/index/procgen-minerl-: We’re excited to announce that OpenAI is co-organizing two NeurIPS 2020 competitions with AIcrowd, Carnegie Mellon University, and DeepMind, using Procgen Benchmark and MineRL.
urls.https://openai.com/index/image-gpt: We find that, just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. By establishing a correlation between sample quality and image classification accuracy, we show that our best generative model also contains features competitive with top convolutional nets in the unsupervised setting.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-api: We’re releasing an API for accessing new AI models developed by OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/ai-and-efficien: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.
urls.https://openai.com/index/jukebox: We’re introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We’re releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.
urls.https://openai.com/index/improving-verif: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.
urls.https://openai.com/index/microscope: We’re introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision “model organisms” which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-pytorch: We are standardizing OpenAI’s deep learning framework on PyTorch.
urls.https://openai.com/index/deep-double-des: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.
urls.https://openai.com/index/procgen-benchma: We’re releasing Procgen Benchmark, 16 simple-to-use procedurally-generated environments which provide a direct measure of how quickly a reinforcement learning agent learns generalizable skills.
urls.https://openai.com/index/safety-gym: We’re releasing Safety Gym, a suite of environments and tools for measuring progress towards reinforcement learning agents that respect safety constraints while training.
urls.https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-1-5b-rele: As the final model release of GPT-2’s staged release, we’re releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.
urls.https://openai.com/index/solving-rubiks-: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: We are now accepting applications for our third class of OpenAI Scholars.
urls.https://openai.com/index/fine-tuning-gpt: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.
urls.https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-u: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.
urls.https://openai.com/index/testing-robustn: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.
urls.https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-6-month-f: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-day: At OpenAI, each Thursday is Learning Day: a day where employees have the option to self-study technical skills that will make them better at their job but which aren’t being learned from daily work.
urls.https://openai.com/index/microsoft-inves: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We’re partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We’ll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider—so we’ll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure’s capabilities in large-scale AI systems.
urls.https://openai.com/index/cooperation-on-: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/symposium-2019: We hosted the first OpenAI Robotics Symposium on April 27, 2019.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: Our second class of OpenAI Scholars has concluded, with all eight scholars producing an exciting final project showcased at Scholars Demo Day at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows-: Our second class of OpenAI Fellows has wrapped up, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship. We are currently reviewing applications on a rolling basis for our next round of OpenAI Fellows Summer 2019.
urls.https://openai.com/index/musenet: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.
urls.https://openai.com/index/sparse-transfor: We’ve developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence—whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-five-def: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind’s AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-five-fin: We’ll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.
urls.https://openai.com/index/energy-based-mo: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-lp: We’ve created OpenAI LP, a new “capped-profit” company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.
urls.https://openai.com/index/introducing-act: We’ve created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.
urls.https://openai.com/index/neural-mmo: We’re releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.
urls.https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/ai-safety-needs: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/better-language: We’ve trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization—all without task-specific training.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-summer-f: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.
urls.https://openai.com/index/how-ai-training: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.
urls.https://openai.com/index/quantifying-gen: We’re releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent’s ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.
urls.https://openai.com/index/spinning-up-in-: We’re releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-concep: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.
urls.https://openai.com/index/reinforcement-l: We’ve developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based method for encouraging reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments through curiosity, which for the first time exceeds average human performance on Montezuma’s Revenge.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-comple: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we’ve decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: We are now accepting applications for our second cohort of OpenAI Scholars, a program where we provide 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows-: We are now accepting applications for OpenAI Fellows and Interns for 2019.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: Our first cohort of OpenAI Scholars has now completed the program.
urls.https://openai.com/index/the-internation: OpenAI Five lost two games against top Dota 2 players at The International in Vancouver this week, maintaining a good chance of winning for the first 20–35 minutes of both games.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben: Yesterday, OpenAI Five won a best-of-three against a team of 99.95th percentile Dota players: Blitz, Cap, Fogged, Merlini, and MoonMeander—four of whom have played Dota professionally—in front of a live audience and 100,000 concurrent livestream viewers.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-dexter: We’ve trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: Our first class of OpenAI Scholars is underway, and you can now follow along as this group of experienced software developers becomes machine learning practitioners.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-five-ben: The OpenAI Five Benchmark match is now over!
urls.https://openai.com/index/glow: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We’re releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-montez: We’ve trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma’s Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-five: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.
urls.https://openai.com/index/retro-contest-r: The first run of our Retro Contest—exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience—is now complete.
urls.https://openai.com/index/language-unsupe: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-fellows: We’re now accepting applications for the next cohort of OpenAI Fellows, a program which offers a compensated 6-month apprenticeship in AI research at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/gym-retro: We’re releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We’re also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.
urls.https://openai.com/index/ai-and-compute: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.
urls.https://openai.com/index/debate: We’re proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.
urls.https://openai.com/index/evolved-policy-: We’re releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.
urls.https://openai.com/index/retro-contest: We’re launching a transfer learning contest that measures a reinforcement learning algorithm’s ability to generalize from previous experience.
urls.https://openai.com/index/hackathon-follo: On March 3rd, we hosted our first hackathon with 100 members of the artificial intelligence community.
urls.https://openai.com/index/reptile: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-scholars: We’re providing 6–10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.
urls.https://openai.com/index/ingredients-for: We’re releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We’ve used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We’re also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-hackatho: Come to OpenAI’s office in San Francisco’s Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.
urls.https://openai.com/index/preparing-for-m: We’ve co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-supporte: We’re excited to welcome new donors to OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/interpretable-m: We’ve designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept—for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs—and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs
urls.https://openai.com/index/discovering-typ: We’ve built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered “types” (non-exclusive categories).
urls.https://openai.com/index/requests-for-re: We’re releasing a new batch of seven unsolved problems which have come up in the course of our research at OpenAI.
urls.https://openai.com/index/block-sparse-gp: We’re releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We’ve used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-a-hier: We’ve developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.
urls.https://openai.com/index/generalizing-fr: Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we’ve used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.
urls.https://openai.com/index/meta-learning-f: We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.
urls.https://openai.com/index/competitive-sel: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.
urls.https://openai.com/index/learning-to-mod: We’re releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner’s dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.
urls.https://openai.com/index/openai-baseline: We’re releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we’ve found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.
urls.https://openai.com/index/more-on-dota-2: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.
urls.https://openai.com/index/dota-2: We’ve created a bot which beats the world’s top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. If that pace holds, within the next two years, most of the code pushed to GitHub could be written by an agent. Much of it may never be fully read by a human. If developers and agents move faster, we have a responsibility to ensure protection keeps up with the accelerated rate of code creation. That means preventing more leaks before they happen and making the response to exposures that remain less dependent on manual human effort. This is a pivotal point for leaked secrets. Developers aren’t becoming more careless; they’re being outpaced. The tools that let developers create more software should also take on more of the work of protecting it. But the quality of existing AI reviewers can be hard to measure, and you need to know the strengths of a reviewer before you know if it will help you. Some reviewers surface more issues, some produce less noise, and some are stronger at catching critical problems while others surface smaller improvements, too. You may need code review to do different things within your workflow. That makes it important to understand how reviewers actually compare: what different systems catch, what they miss, and the tradeoffs they make. A good code review benchmark should reflect the diversity of real pull requests, capture a broad set of review findings, and support meaningful breakdowns by severity, category, and precision-recall preferences. For teams building code review agents, the benchmark should also provide an offline signal that reliably tracks whether changes are likely to improve the experience in production. Both need v2.1.290 or later Added $.prompt.media so a prompt.submit hook of a mod installed by managed settings can read the bytes of an image or document attached to the prompt Added $.session.identity() for mods installed by managed settings: how the session is signed in, and its organization and email when managed forceLoginOrgUUID lists that organization Added size, weight, mono and tabular to a mod's Text and named spacing steps (xs to xl) to its Box; bold is deprecated in favor of weight Added --shutdown-drain-sec to claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator: on SIGTERM it stops polling and gives the poll in flight and running spawn hooks up to that many seconds to finish Added the skill's frontmatter, source, plugin name and file path to what a mod's skill.prompt hook receives Added /effort and /fast in agent view to set what new sessions start with; a bare /model, /effort or /fast there now opens a picker Added a "safe mode" line to the agents view peek panel for bac

What's changed Added a code key to the Claude apps gateway's managed.policies[]: the same settings as cli, also applied in Claude Desktop's Code tab; beside desktop, it turns on Claude Desktop's gateway mode Added autoCompactWindow to subagent frontmatter and --agents definitions, so a subagent can auto-compact earlier than the main conversation's window Added CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL to run every workflow agent on one model while other subagents keep theirs Added CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS environment variable to set a longer maximum delay for the backoff when retrying an overloaded (529) request Added a note in /plugin on a plugin whose hooks are left out because another enabled plugin has the same name Added an allow_large option to the Read tool so Claude can read a text file past the usual size limits in one call when it needs the whole file and the context has room Fixed managed-settings PreToolUse hooks that deny a tool call with "continue": false, and managed prompt hooks that block one, refusing the call but not ending the turn Fixed PostToolUse hooks in managed settings not applying updatedMCPToolOutput in some sessions Fixed headless sessions starting a folder's .mcp.json or plugin MCP server that was switched off for that folder, after changing directory or reloading plugins Fixed a Claude apps gateway that serves allowedProviders with "gateway" locking out laptops that name that gateway in user settings Fixed a saved Claude apps gateway

What's changed Added onFailure: "block" for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can't start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through Added Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501) support: terminals that implement it can show whether Claude Code is working, waiting on you, or done Added quoted text to the /copy picker, so a drafted message copies without its > markers Added a warning to claude plugin install, enable, disable and marketplace add when the settings file they write to does not load Added a line on stderr, when it is a terminal, that says what a claude -p run is waiting for when it stays open after its last turn Added support for timeouts.upstream_ttfb_ms on the Claude apps gateway's Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and other cloud upstreams: a value you set now limits how long a stream may take to start there, after which it fails over or gets a 502 Added a "Backgrounding cancelled" message when you stop the turn while ← is waiting for the current tool to finish Added an optional models list to every Claude apps gateway upstream: only the listed models are sent there, on failover too, and one * in an entry is a wildcard Added support for forceLoginMethod: "gateway" and forceLoginGatewayUrl in your own user settings on machines with no managed settings, so /login opens on that Claude apps gateway Added advice to claude plugin validate when a plugin's README has no install line: it prints the line to paste and never changes the

What's changed Fixed prompt and agent hooks written as instructions (such as "Block commands that...") allowing what they should block Improved how prompt hooks on Stop and SubagentStop written as instructions (such as "Carry on if the build is broken") are judged, so Claude is less likely to stop early

What's changed Added Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), now the default Haiku model on the Anthropic API — 1M context, $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok ($0.50/$2.50 for prompts over 100K) Added agentType to the subagentStatusLine payload, so scripts can tell custom subagent types apart Added isDeferred to $.tool.register for mods: false lists the tool's schema in the prompt from the start instead of behind tool search Fixed Claude sometimes treating its own last actions before a context compaction as done after it, and retracting or redoing finished work Fixed a memory leak where an HTTP MCP connection kept every request it had sent until it closed Fixed a message sent while Claude was working being lost when ← moved the session to the background; if a queued message can't move, ← now stays put and says so Fixed /model effort ←/→ wrapping past the highest or lowest level, which could accidentally save Low as a model's default effort Fixed /tui disconnecting Claude in Chrome in a session started with --chrome, and ignoring --no-chrome Fixed Claude being told to continue or message subagents with SendMessage in sessions, including resumed ones, where a host, a permission rule or a --tools list removed that tool Fixed subagents and --agent sessions being told a built-in tool was disabled for the whole session when only their own tool list left it out Fixed a claude.ai-synced skill's edited description sometimes not reaching the model until a new conversation or /clear Fixed claude logs, s

What's changed Added --marketplace to claude plugin install: adds the marketplace if needed, under the same policy checks as claude plugin marketplace add, then installs the plugin from it Added an effort parameter to the Agent tool, so Claude runs a sub-agent at the effort level you ask for Added CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS environment variable to set a longer base delay for the backoff when retrying an overloaded (529) request Added prompt.autocomplete, an event a mod hooks to add its own rows to the prompt box's autocomplete list Added prompt caching to $.model.complete for mods: prompt and system take blocks of text, and cache: true on a block caches the request up to it Added workflow agents to the agent.spawn mod hook, with their run and index, so a mod can refuse them Fixed subagent definitions with permissionMode: auto entering auto mode when auto mode is unavailable (disabled by settings, circuit breaker, or a model that doesn't support it) Fixed sandboxed commands being able to read the staged file copies of /ultrareview uploads under ~/.claude/seed-admin Fixed a managed sandbox read-deny path (and user ones beside it) that appears or re-points mid-session not dropping project grants inside it or ending credential injection from files it covers Fixed a notebook or PDF read on macOS and Windows being able to return a file outside what was approved, through a link swapped in mid-read Fixed a tampered on-disk cache of server-managed settings being able t

What's changed Fixed a regression in 2.1.290 where cloud sessions could drop answers to permission prompts Fixed a regression in 2.1.288 where the last messages of a session could be lost when quitting

What's changed Added serverToolUses to the result of a mod's turn.step hook: the tool calls the API ran itself (the advisor), each with its id, name, input, start and end Added agentId to the tool.check event of plugin hooks, so a hook can tell a subagent's permission check from the main session's Added ceiling to the question and verdict a mod's tool.check hook reads, naming the approval an organization requires for a tool Added ThemeKey and Color types to the plugin hooks typings, so an editor lists the theme colors a mod's drawing can name Added to claude plugin validate: each hook a mod registers at a gating site is listed with whether it has a .catch (gatingHooks under --json) Added a Deny button to the Claude apps gateway's sign-in approval page: it ends the pending sign-in, so the waiting terminal stops within seconds Added claude attach and claude logs : part of a session name works in place of the id Added /claude-api managed-agents-onboard to set up the Managed Agents pattern a page describes as ant apply files Added /claude-api managed-agents-onboard to build a Console quickstart template, such as deep-researcher, with the ant CLI Added a warning when a managed settings file is a link to a file outside the managed settings folder Added a /status and doctor warning when managed settings ignore user-configured sandbox allowRead paths or allowed domains Fixed requests failing behind proxies and gateways that reject one of Claude Code's beta headers with a status other

What's changed Fixed a deny or ask rule on a nested part of a compound shell command not holding over a user-installed mod's approval on managed machines Fixed the terminal freezing on short code blocks with many unclosed tags or deeply nested ${ substitutions Fixed Read deny rules not applying to files @-mentioned, changed, or selected in the IDE through a symlink [VSCode] Reverted a 2.1.288 change to claude auth status that may have made sign-outs more frequent Improved how quickly large files open in a plugin code pane by laying the highlighted view out once at its final width Fixed plugin list, plugin eval and plugin update showing a stale copy of a plugin installed from a local folder marketplace, and hot reload for a symlinked --plugin-dir Fixed installed mods not loading in the first session after an upgrade Fixed a plugin's rows above the prompt showing a stale row while the Background tasks dialog was open in fullscreen Fixed plugin panes drawing nothing when a link used a localhost address, an @ in its path, an uppercase host or a file: path Fixed a user-installed plugin being able to rewrite the descriptions of an organization-managed MCP server's sign-in tools Fixed a freeze or forced quit at launch when a plugin drew a Box with a border style the terminal does not know Fixed supervised and background sessions ending when a plugin's on-screen handler threw asynchronously Fixed sessions ending with an interface error when a plugin region with no height kept growing

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/610.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据科技媒体 TechRadar 今天报道，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋近期在伦敦的 Build a Claw 活动认为，OpenClaw 将推动未来科技发展，特别是机器人领域。 黄仁勋首先指出，OpenClaw 是迄今为止最重要的模型之一，有助于多个行业进步。他对此解释称：“我们已经看到人工智能迎来转折点，它开始变得实用。人们正在用 AI 做各种事情，从简单的软件编程，到担任营销代理、研究助理和实验室助理、药物研发，如今到处都有智能体。” IT之家从原报道获悉，黄仁勋看到合作伙伴 Humanoid 的机器人后认为，OpenClaw 是“首个真正可信的智能体运行框架”。他认为 OpenClaw 就像外骨骼的大语言模型，应用在机器人领域可能带来许多好处。 他说道：“OpenClaw 刚推出时，我就觉得它是非常出色的数字机器人系统。它有点像具身智能，本质是为 LLM 提供了实时运行框架。电机、关节、车轮和机械臂都只是工具，最终要由电脑运行的智能体操控。” “这种情况与互联网早期很相似。当时浏览器并未与计算机隔离，用户访问网站时，这些 Web 页面可能会下载应用程序，并获得对底层硬件的完全控制权，而且还会向用户的电脑推送它所说的「特殊软件包」。” “最显而易见的解决方法就是建立容器，也就是隔离层，本质上是在操作系统内部再运行一个 OS。因此我们开发了 OpenShell 系统。当你开发一个自主系统时，首先应该假设任何对象都不可信，仅授予最低权限。例如你让一个自主系统做煎蛋，就没必要给它电锯，它只需要一口煎锅。” 关于 AI 智能体失控的论调，黄仁勋比较乐观，他认为权限管控是必要的：“我们会持续监控这些自主系统。如果机器人违反规则，或者做出超出权限范围的行动，系统就会发出警报。我们可以决定是否让它闭嘴。”

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/608.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，《雾锁王国》（Enshrouded）结束近三年的抢先体验阶段，1.0 正式版今日正式上线，登陆 PC（Steam）和 PlayStation 5 平台（PS5 与 PS5 Pro 版本目标 60 帧运行），但 Xbox Series X|S 版本已推迟至 2027 年春季。 据 Keen Games 官方公告，Xbox 版延期是因开发团队认为需要额外时间才能达到其期望的质量与性能表现。 IT之家注：1.0 版本首发暂不支持跨平台联机，开发团队表示正在为此努力，但暂无法预估所需时间。 国区定价方面，Steam 标准版售价 138 元，原声音乐 28 元，游戏支持简体中文。据 Steam 商店页面信息，1.0 版对旧存档完全兼容，玩家无需重新开始。 不过需要注意的是，所有角色的技能树将在首次进入 1.0 版本时被重置，自定义按键绑定也会恢复默认设置，因为 1.0 新增了大量控制选项。抢先体验期间参与游戏的玩家将获得专属奖励。 1.0 版本最核心的内容是完整地图的解锁。新区域“余烬摇篮”位于北方，穿过帷幕水盆地后开启的大门即可进入。该区域分为上下两层：下层是熔岩流淌的荒芜之地，散落着神秘过往的遗迹，部分地区被瘴气吞噬；上层则是远古人抬升大地后打造的浮空岛屿国度，充满奇特生物、精巧建筑和毫不留情的守护者。两层世界之间由不断向上蔓延的瘴气触须相连。此外，阿尔班耶夫山脉和帷幕水盆地各新增一座空荡礼堂，春日平原、黑沼和燃火荒原等既有生态区域也向世界边缘大幅扩展。 等级与成长系统随之扩展。玩家等级上限从抢先体验版的 45 级提升至 50 级，装备最高可升级至 55 级。火焰祭坛数量上限提升至 15 座，击败最终 Boss 后还可额外解锁一个火焰等级，使火焰祭坛能在过去无法触及的瘴气区域绽放。一位精通远古知识与配方的新幸存者将加入玩家基地，解锁新一阶的制作内容，包括新装备、工具、食物、消耗品、箭矢与法术，以及新的家具、摆件、建筑方块和植物。 战斗系统的调整是 1.0 的另一重点。法师职业获得显著加强，共新增 9 种法术：吸取法力（Mana Drain）、缠绕（Entangle）、烈焰之柱（Pillar of Flames）、暴风雪（Blizzard）、球状闪电（Ball Lightning），以及四种全新的召唤法术 —— 火焰图腾、寒冰图腾、电击图腾和空洞骷髅。召唤法术是 1.0 引入的全新法术类别，技能树中新增了两个技能用于提升可召唤的骷髅和图腾数量。魔杖战斗也得到重做，新增重击攻击，可穿透敌人并打断弱敌的攻击动作；同时加入空中魔杖攻击和魔杖闪避攻击两项新技能。永恒法术（不消耗法术弹药）现在可以像武器和护甲一样升级，获得独特的新增益效果。 基地建造系统新增 Sparkworks 逻辑系统，玩家可以用它制作可互动的内容，并通过分享平台交流。该系统的完整版本扩展了陷阱、生成器和逻辑元件，理论上允许玩家在游戏中构建自定义地牢。世界中所有的背景故事笔记、信件和书籍现在提供完整的英文、德文和中文配音，玩家可以像听有声书一样收听背景故事，还能将多篇笔记加入播放列表依次播放。 据 Keen Games 创意总监 Antony Christoulakis 透露，游戏玩家数已超过 500 万。该作于 2024 年 1 月 24 日进入 Steam 抢先体验，四天内售出 100 万份，同年 8 月销量超过 300 万份，鼎盛时期 Steam 同时在线玩家数达到 160,405 人。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/604.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据韩媒 The Elec 今天报道，SK 海力士现已公布 3D FeNAND 实现模拟存内计算（Analog Compute-in-Memory，A-CiM）的研究成果，相关研究已发表于 IEEE 论文。 据介绍，A-CiM 可利用模拟信号直接在存储器执行乘积累加运算（IT之家注：MAC），减少数据搬运、提升处理速度和能效。 3D FeNAND 则利用铁电材料的极化状态存储数据并控制电流。对比之下，传统 3D NAND 采用电荷俘获氮化物（CTN）结构，将电子捕获在氮化物层中。铁电材料的特点是，即使外部电场消失，其内部极化状态仍能保持。 SK 海力士表示，FeNAND 可在单个存储单元内产生多种电流状态，适合 AI 计算所需的权重数据。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/598.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，英伟达创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋近日到访中国台湾，麻省理工学院 AI 研究员莱克斯 · 弗里德曼（Lex Fridman）与其同行，并用镜头记录下了完整的一日行程。相关视频已于当地时间 10 月 14 日发布在 YouTube 等平台上。 在谈及中国台湾的半导体产业链时，黄仁勋表示，去年令他感到欣慰的并非英伟达自身股价大涨，而是整条供应链相关企业股价大幅上涨，英伟达自身股价反而保持平稳。在他看来，这意味着英伟达搭建的产业平台能够带动上下游伙伴共同成长，实现生态整体繁荣。 黄仁勋在访谈中明确表达了自己的商业哲学：做生意切忌只顾自己吃尽全部利润，将合作伙伴压榨到无利可图。他提出，如果企业逼迫供应商为订单恶意竞价，只顾自身赚取收益，这种行事方式会在行业内留下长久印记，行业圈子都会记住这家企业的做法。 黄仁勋强调，做生意要永远把一部分利益留在桌面上，顾及合作方的生存与收益。“只有合作伙伴同样能够赚到钱，双方的业务合作才具备长期稳固的基础。” 这套理念贯穿了黄仁勋对英伟达与台积电三十余年合作关系的回顾。他回忆了 1996 年联系台积电的曲折经历：翻黄页、反复拨打美国办公室电话、留下语音却始终没有收到回电，最后给张忠谋写了一封长信。直到某天傍晚六点左右，办公室外员工正在玩初代 PlayStation，电话那头传来一句：“我是台积电的张忠谋。”黄仁勋当时喊道：“嘿，大家安静！张忠谋打电话来了！”他坦言，那一刻他想到的是“也许我们不用倒闭了”。 谈及为何最终选择台积电而非联电，黄仁勋表示，张忠谋有一点特别打动他：当他提出很多要求时，张忠谋会明确告诉他“这件事我们做不了”，但随后会补上一句“Jensen，如果我们合作，我向你保证，我们将为你想办法、克服困难”。 “三十年来，他们一直在兑现这句话。”黄仁勋说，这背后是对经营边界、诚信和长期关系的坚持。芯片制造充满了未知，不可能提前约定所有细节，“你真正选择的，不是买什么，而是和谁一起做”。 黄仁勋还以“粗暴正义”来形容这段合作关系：不可能每次都完全公平，有时他们多得一点，有时我多得一点，但把时间拉长，最终都不吃亏。“他们必须知道，你希望他们成功。每一天，台积电都知道，我希望他们能获得成功。” 在谈到中国 AI 公司时，黄仁勋认为，算力限制反而逼着这些公司把架构做到极致。“他们受到的限制非常、非常大”，但仍在获得融资、继续推进，“拼命把事情搞清楚”。他将此概括为“限制是发明之母，资源稀缺会催生创新”。 IT之家注意到，在此次访谈中，双方也穿插了不少个人化的片段。黄仁勋回忆起五岁时在台湾夜市被厨师的刀划伤脸、父亲抱着他跑去医院的经历，也谈到小时候家里没钱去餐馆，只能逛夜市坐在桌旁吃饭。 他说，每个人都在努力谋生，工作那么辛苦，却还是想拿出一点东西与你分享，“他们把利润都让给了我，只是想表达一份善意”。 他还提到，英伟达在中国台湾的本地团队约有一千人，涵盖芯片设计、系统工程、运营工程以及晶圆制造、封装和测试等环节，公司计划新建一栋可容纳四千人的大楼，再招募三千人。 相关阅读： 《英伟达黄仁勋谈 EVGA：CEO 安德鲁是很好的朋友，而他早就有离开显卡市场的想法》 《剑指老黄、不服就干：EVGA 怒喷英伟达，宣誓从此不再生产新显卡》

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/591.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据雷峰网报道，因在 618 大促期间发朋友圈造谣诋毁其他平台，京东公司采销经理左琦被抖音电商起诉。目前，北京市海淀区人民法院已正式立案。 据回顾，2026 年 5 月 29 日至 31 日，一张京东采销经理左琦发布的朋友圈截图在社交媒体广泛传播，大量社交媒体账号发帖称“京东员工朋友圈曝抖音裹挟商家媒体、黑京东就有流量”。相关内容在社交平台的发布时间集中、内容同质化严重、IP 地址集中，具有明显的水军特征，发布后还被多家媒体误信，进行了援引报道。 左琦在朋友圈称，618 大促前夕，不少商家和媒体都收到了某平台公开指责京东的要求，该平台会给京东的负面新闻流量扶持，并在仅有一条媒体报道的基础上，将京东的负面新闻推上了自家的热榜。上述指控同时配有一张带有今日头条链接的截图，来说明所谓的“某平台”是在指代抖音电商和今日头条。 据悉，所谓流量扶持京东负面等指控纯属捏造，左琦朋友圈配图中的链接，对应的是一篇官方媒体的行业监督报道，名为“知名电商平台陷乱价风波：同款电器差价超千元，市监部门要求落实内卷式竞争整治”，该报道从未登上过今日头条热榜。 该报道指出，京东平台往往会在大促期间要求平台内商家必须提供“全网最低价”、降价成本主要由商家承担，同时通过“毛利保护”条款保障自身利润；为了竞争，京东有时还会针对自己几乎无货的其他平台专供品，故意标一个很低的价格来“乱价”，同款电器有时和其他平台差价上千元，“本质上是用一个假的价格，去干扰商家在其他平台的销售”。 报道认为，上述行为违反了《互联网平台价格行为规则》中关于“平台不得强制或者变相强制平台内经营者降价”的有关规定，也和监管部门“内卷式”竞争综合整治的精神相悖。 IT之家查询获悉，捏造、散布涉竞争对手的虚假信息，损害其商业信誉的，构成名誉权侵权或者商业诋毁，需要承担损害赔偿、赔礼道歉等民事责任；造成重大损失或者有其他严重情节的，甚至可能构成损害商业信誉、商品声誉罪，面临有期徒刑、拘役、罚金等刑事责任。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/586.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，飞牛 fnOS 今日发布了每周一次的周四更新，飞牛素材库 Seek 新增多语言支持、视频分辨率筛选等功能，同时飞牛相册独立 App 的内测招募也正式启动。 据飞牛官方社区公告，独立相册 App 内测招募面向手机中存有大量照片需要长期自动备份、家中有多人共同查看照片需求、拥有数万甚至数十万张照片的用户。 飞牛官方还在公告中解释了开发独立相册的初衷：随着用户照片数量增长，相册已不只是设备管理中的一个附属功能，快速打开、随时备份、顺畅浏览和轻松查找回忆，都需要更专注的使用体验。独立相册 App 将围绕照片备份、浏览、整理和家庭使用场景进行优化，相比功能更全面的飞牛主 App，独立相册打开更直接，进入 App 即可查看照片，减少操作路径，也方便不熟悉 NAS 管理功能的家庭成员使用。此次内测将重点验证独立 App 是否真的比主 App 中的相册更方便、更稳定、更适合日常高频使用。 飞牛素材库 Seek 此次更新支持简体中文、英语、日语、德语、法语和西班牙语六种语言，视频预览新增 6K、8K、12K 分辨率区分，并支持按视频分辨率筛选素材。此外，更新修复了项目创建者被删除后无法访问的问题，并新增压缩文件解压能力。 配合此次更新，飞牛同步推出 Seek 采集插件，支持将网页图片和视频一键存入素材库，项目批量采集时会保留素材来源信息。 IT之家获悉，Seek 是飞牛 fnOS 于今年 8 月推出的官方媒体资产管理应用，面向视频工作室、自媒体团队等创作者群体，以项目维度统一管理音视频和图片素材，内置专业播放器支持多格式在线预览与自动转码，并提供多人协同审片、锚点评论、版本管理及带权限的外部分享链接等功能。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/578.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，江波龙今日发布 2026 年三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）业绩预告报告： 营业总收入：380 亿元 ~400 亿元，同比增长 127.08%~139.03% 归母净利润：140 亿元 ~149 亿元，同比增长 1864.55%~1990.84% 扣非净利润：138 亿元 ~148 亿元，同比增长 2782.36%~2991.23% 资产负债率：50% AI 解读 本次业绩预告归母净利润和营收增速均大幅超出市场一致预期，业绩表现亮眼。 公司主营业务与财报亮点 江波龙是国内专注于消费级、工业级、车规级存储产品的研发、生产和销售的龙头企业，产品覆盖 UFS、SSD、ePOP 等多个高端存储领域。 2026 年前三季度，公司预计实现营业收入 380 亿元 ～ 400 亿元，上年同期为 167.34 亿元；实现归属于上市公司股东的净利润 140 亿元 ～ 149 亿元，同比增长 1864.55% ～ 1990.84% ，上年同期净利润为 7.13 亿元；扣除非经常性损益后净利润 138 亿元 ～ 148 亿元，同比增长 2782.36% ～ 2991.23% ，上年同期扣非净利润为 4.79 亿元。 单季度来看，2026 年第三季度公司实现营业收入 139 亿元 ～ 159 亿元，同比增长 112.76% ～ 145.35% ；实现扣除非经常性损益后净利润 37.53 亿元 ～ 47.53 亿元，同比增长 740.33% ～ 964.26% ，盈利能力维持历史较高水平。 第三季度公司实现经营性现金流量净额转正，期末资产负债率低于 50%，经营健康度进一步提升。 行业变动与公司进展 全球存储器市场供需格局整体偏紧，但受前期较高价格基数影响，DRAM 和 NAND Flash 价格涨幅较前期明显收窄，存储价格上涨对盈利的边际贡献趋缓，行业正从消费类价格周期转向 AI 驱动技术周期。 公司以自研芯片、自研软件架构为技术引领，走差异化发展路线，大客户、高端客户及全球化客户占比持续提升，产品与客户结构进一步优化。 技术创新持续突破，UFS 4.1、mSSD、ePOP5x 等高端新产品已在知名大客户实现规模化商用，国际化业务保持高速增长；端侧 AI 技术合作范围进一步拓展至 AMD、高通等全球知名企业，成长空间持续打开。 风险提示 本次业绩为初步测算结果，未经审计机构审计，具体数据请以后续正式披露的三季报为准，投资者请注意业绩波动风险。 相关阅读： 《复旦微电 2026 年三季度归母净利润 9.5 亿元 ~11.5 亿元，同比 187.63%~248.18%》 《台积电 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 7630.64 亿新台币，同比增长 68.7%》 《阿斯麦 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 49.6 亿欧元，同比增长 133.49%》 《江波龙 2026 年上半年归母净利润 105.77 亿元，同比增长 71528.66%》 《江波龙：预计 2026 年上半年归母净利润 92 亿元～ 110 亿元，同比预增 62204%~74394%》 《江波龙 2026 年一季度净利润 38.62 亿元，同比增长 2644.05%》 风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/521.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，Instagram 用户 wilcoblok 昨日拍到了一款伪装成奥迪的保时捷 Macan 原型车。Autocar 今日放出了更多关于这款车的谍照。 该车虽然披着奥迪 Q5 的车身外壳，但加宽的轮拱、外扩的轮距以及更高的姿态，表明其壳下并非 Q5，而是同平台的保时捷 Macan 燃油车型。 保时捷正在为计划于 2028 年推出的燃油及插电混动 SUV 进行动力总成和底盘调校工作，新车预计将与现有的 Macan 纯电车型并行销售，而非取代后者。 从谍照细节来看，测试车前脸换装了全新的格栅设计，舍弃了奥迪 Q5 标志性的网状进气格栅，前保险杠两侧和中央位置设有大面积进气口，后方可见散热器，暗示其动力系统不容小觑。 其车尾配备了取自老款 Macan 的双边共四出排气，进一步印证了 V6 发动机的存在。轮拱周围和底盘下方安装的泡沫块，是保时捷在每台原型车上用于验证真实路况下离地间隙的常规做法，这些泡沫块表明新车的坐姿将显著低于且宽于 Q5，从而获得更强的动态性能。 据 Autocar 报道，这款燃油 SUV 将基于与奥迪 Q5 相同的 PPC（Premium Platform Combustion）高端平台打造，这也解释了测试车为何在外观上与 Q5 高度一致。 不过，保时捷尚未确认其未来燃油 SUV 的底层架构。借用 Q5 车身可以让工程师在最终设计仍隐藏在临时面板和泡沫块之下的情况下，进行真实耐久性和标定工作。 保时捷设计负责人 Tobias Suhlmann 近期暗示，新车的外观将与 Macan 纯电车型有明显区别：“首先，它看起来应该是一台保时捷。我们讨论过鱼雷式翼子板，在 SUV 上你也应该能看到它们。” 动力系统方面，早期爆料信息表明这款新车将采用涡轮增压四缸和 V6 发动机，还将提供至少一款插电混动版本，并很可能作为顶配 Turbo 车型出现。 也有不同的报道称，测试车搭载的是一台 4.0 升 V8 双涡轮增压发动机，内部代号“EA825 evo”，但这一说法目前未获保时捷官方证实。 在 10 月 7 日 2026 年市场日上，保时捷正式公布了“Sportswagenschmiede 35”新品战略，其中包括一款定位在 911 之上的新旗舰超级跑车、一款全新的燃油 SUV 以及纯电动的 718 系列。 保时捷 CEO 骆明楷（Michael Leiters）曾表示，燃油及插电混动 Macan“计划于 2028 年进入市场”，并将缩小 718 和燃油 Macan 当前的产品空白列为保时捷的当务之急。 骆明楷 9 月 30 日接受英国《金融时报》采访时指出，上半年 Macan 电动版销量同比下滑 40%，而燃油版仍录得正增长。 IT之家提醒：这款燃油 SUV 是否会沿用 Macan 之名目前尚无定论。Macan 这一徽标目前与基于 PPE 平台打造的电动车型紧密绑定，因此新车可能以全新身份亮相，即便爱好者们出于习惯仍称其为燃油 Macan。 此前燃油版 Macan 的生产已于 2026 年 7 月结束，但它在第三季度的销量仍达到 27996 辆，超过了电动版的 23029 辆。骆明楷表示，目标是在 2028 年燃油 Macan 推出后，为客户提供一个在电动和燃油之间均衡的选择。 相关阅读： 《保时捷 CEO 骆明楷：2028 年将推出燃油版 Macan，重拾油车≠弃电动化》

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/475.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，OpenCode 刚刚宣布，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 现已免费提供，免费版实测支持 200K 上下文窗口，相比 1M 上下文版本有所降低。 此次免费开放是在此前“Operation Cheepseek”计划基础上的进一步动作。今年 9 月，OpenCode 曾将 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 在 OpenCode Go 套餐中的使用额度从 15 美元临时提升至 60 美元，随后于 10 月 12 日将该额度调整为 80 美元。此次免费开放后，该模型在 OpenCode 平台内的调用不再计入额度消耗。 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 于 2026 年 9 月 10 日正式发布，是一款原生多模态 MoE 模型，主干参数规模为 552B，另含 196B Engram 条件记忆参数。IT之家注意到，其架构采用因果编码器-解码器设计，40 层语言主干中前 20 层为因果编码器、后 20 层为解码器，Prefill 计算量接近减半。该模型在 DeepSeek 官方平台上并无免费 API 层级，计费采用预充值按量付费方式。 在用户反馈方面，生成速度（TPS）的表现是社区讨论的焦点。多位用户报告了较大的速度波动。有用户称在 ollama 云平台上最高曾观察到约 490 tokens/s 的输出速度，但整体不稳定，中午至下午时段最低可降至五六十 tokens/s。 在 OpenCode Go 套餐内，亦有用户反映 TPS 掉至 100 以下。此外，社区测试显示速度会随上下文增长而下降，有用户报告上下文超过 100K 后 TPS 降至不足 100，达到 200K 时约为 50 tokens/s 左右。 相关阅读： 《OpenCode 宣布为 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 永久提供 60 美元额度》 《DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 模型正式发布：全面超越 V4 Pro、原生多模态视觉理解，最高降价 60%》 《DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5 更新：适配 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 模型，新增文件上传与侧边栏预览功能》

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/473.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，Omdia 英国当地时间今日根据其初步估计表示，全球智能手机出货量在 2026 年第 3 季度出现了 20% 的同比下滑，衰退幅度较 Q2 的 6% 显著扩大。 ▲ 图源：Omdia 而从季对季的角度看，尽管多家制造商都在 2026Q3 发布了旗舰新品，但全球的智能手机出货量在环比层面仍出现了萎缩。 ▲ 图源：Omdia 机构认为，持续的存储器成本压力限制了智能手机品牌的定价灵活性，迫使厂商缩减低利润设备的出货量。供应商正优先考虑 ASP 的增长和产品组合的优化，以维持出货价值并保障盈利能力。 与此同时，智能手机市场的两极分化进一步加剧：三星和苹果分别拿下 23% 和 22% 出货，两者合计市占相较去年同期上升了 8 个百分点；其后是小米的 12%、OPPO 的 9%、vivo 的 8%。 ▲ 图源：Omdia 参考 Omdia: Global smartphone market shrinks 20% in 3Q26 as memory crisis reshapes competition
urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/472.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，大麦 APP 今日就《2026 肖战“出口 · 我们”巡回演唱会-南京站》开票后出现的“天价票”传闻作出回应，明确表示相关网络信息为黄牛在无任何票源情况下的恶意炒作，大麦强烈抵制并已将相关线索提交有关部门。 据上海证券报报道，南京站两场演出于当日 10:05 在大麦 APP 独家预售，开票后迅速售罄，期间参与抢票人数超过 500 万，平台瞬时访问量大幅攀升，整体运行平稳。 此前有网传截图显示，南京站内场 1960 元档门票被炒至 25 万元一张。大麦网公示的可售票总数为两场共计 22020 张，而开票前单站“想看”人数已突破 500 万，创下 2026 年内地演唱会最高纪录，中签率不足 0.5%。 肖战工作室已于 10 月 14 日发布购票提醒，明确本次演唱会不存在“内部票”“员工票”“合作方预留票”，并特别提醒黄牛手中的票很可能是他人已实名绑定的，即使加价购得也无法入场，加价款项亦难以追回。 为从源头压缩黄牛操作空间，大麦演出实行全流程“强实名”政策。门票与观演人身份信息绑定，购票成功后不可转赠、不可更改观演人信息，每个账号最多购买 2 张。入场时将严格核验比对观演人身份证原件、电子票及人脸信息，三项信息全部一致方可入场，除大麦官方核验流程外无任何其他入场方式。 据澎湃新闻报道，肖战工作室在与大麦签订合同时，主动放弃了行业惯例中主办方可保留的 15% 内部票源，将所有可售票投入公开票池。 大麦方面同时表示，平台已启动高级别安全防御机制，系统将实时识别并拦截使用虚假设备、不安全插件、外挂软件及网络代理等恶意抢票行为，坚决打击“黑灰产”刷票及黄牛倒卖，一经发现将依据平台规则取消相关订单并依法追究责任。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/467.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，在今天举行的商务部例行新闻发布会上，新闻发言人就中欧在混动汽车领域达成的谅解作出回应。 商务部新闻发言人何亚东表示，双方在混动汽车领域达成的谅解是对等互利的，是基于双方在世贸组织规则框架下强调并确认的三大原则，也就是全流程合规、尊重事实和非歧视。有关共识有力维护了中国企业的实际利益，避免了中欧贸易摩擦局面升级。这充分说明，中欧通过基于规则的共识而进行了磋商，不仅能够解决问题，而且会深化互利合作，推动中欧贸易向上平衡、向前发展。 据IT之家此前报道，2026 年 10 月 8-9 日，中国商务部部长王文涛与欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什 · 谢夫乔维奇在北京举行中欧贸易投资磋商机制（以下简称机制）第二次例会。经密集磋商，中欧双方以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解。 另外，14 日午间，中国汽车工业协会发布《中国汽车工业协会关于中欧混动汽车、电动汽车磋商共识的声明》。声明提到，近日，中欧双方秉持相互尊重、平等协商的原则，在贸易投资磋商机制下就混动汽车、电动汽车贸易问题开展了密集磋商并达成共识。中国汽车工业协会对此高度关注，并对磋商取得的积极成果表示欢迎和支持。

urls.https://ithome.com/1/013/461.htm: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，今日红魔正式发布了新一代电竞旗舰红魔 12 Pro+，新机今日 18:00 现货开售，提供氘锋透明暗夜、氘锋透明银翼、氘锋透明冰蓝三款透明配色，发布会现场还展示了“红魔 12 PRO+ GOLDEN SAGA 臻金传奇 · 限量典藏”特别版本，提供 24GB+1TB 版本。 IT之家注意到，售价方面，12GB+256GB 官方价 6999 元、16GB+512GB 为 7999 元、16GB+1TB 为 8999 元；叠加国家补贴后到手价分别为 6499 元、7499 元、8499 元。 红魔 12 Pro+ 延续品牌标志性的透明设计与机甲美学，机身采用红魔独家纯平背板，官方称横握游戏时“纯平不挡手、更顺手”；背部使用独家一体化镜片后盖，主打镜片级透光、耐磨与抗刮花。标准版与 Pro+ 的背部排布进一步简化，官方称“更简约、更高级”。 新机背部延续“红魔透明”的设计血统，并把水冷系统做成可视化：透明美学配合双环水冷，中央 RGB 灯环可随灯效点亮。红魔称其为行业首款 RGB 水冷，宣传语为“RGB 一开，性能提升 200%”。 新机搭载安卓阵营唯一真全面屏，红魔联合 BOE（京东方）定制“国屏之光”，搭载第九代屏下技术，透光率更高、刷新率更高、边框更窄，边框窄至 0.96mm。官方将屏下全面屏称为“电竞玩家杀手锏”，视野无遮挡。 红魔回顾称其长期领跑高刷赛道：2019 年红魔 3 首发 90Hz，2020 年红魔 5G 首发 144Hz，2021 年红魔 6 首发 165Hz；此次红魔 12 Pro+ 带来行业首款 185Hz 全面屏，并向下兼容 165Hz，已有 185Hz 游戏高刷适配。屏幕还行业首发超高刷显示芯片 G1（22nm 制程），以及屏下 X11 发光材料，官方称亮度更高、功耗更低、寿命更长。 触控与自拍方面，新机采用新思 Synaptics Byrd 触控芯片，支持 5000Hz 瞬时触控采样率与 500Hz 全局触控采样率，并搭载 MagicTouch 4.0 触控算法，官方数据为滑动响应提升 33%、连击响应提升 28%。护眼上配备星盾护眼技术 2.0，通过 SGS 低蓝光护眼认证。前置为 1600 万像素屏下摄像头，配合 AI 去炫光 / 去雾等算法，覆盖屏下认证、扫脸支付、前置自拍与视频通话场景。 性能上，红魔 12 Pro+ 采用“电竞双芯”：第六代骁龙 8 超级至尊版 + 红魔自研红芯 R5。其中主芯片为台积电 2nm 工艺，最高主频 5GHz，官方称 GPU 性能提升 44%；安兔兔性能跑分达到 5,670,006，位居第一。红芯 R5 自研电竞芯片负责触控优化、光效控制、光帧追踪与超分超帧。 红魔还行业首发“红魔自研全场景光线追踪”，官方称画面更加真实、细节更多，并首发支持六款主流游戏；同时可与超分、超帧“三视效并发”。此外，《穿越火线：枪战王者》支持原生 185Hz；官方称 10 款主流游戏支持 2K+185Hz 超分超帧并发，200 多款主流游戏支持超分 / 超帧。 借助红魔 PC 模拟器，官方提出“引领手机进入 3A 级性能时代”：模拟器全新改版，支持 Steam 创意工坊、按键与布局重构、Steam 成就数据展示与更直观的参数自定义。红魔 12 Pro+ 演示《古墓丽影 9》平均 60.1 FPS、《孤岛惊魂 3》平均 120 FPS 稳帧畅玩；红魔同时宣布获得育碧游戏工作室官方认证。发布会也提示游戏手柄需单独购买。 赛事层面，红魔 12 Pro+ 成为英雄联盟手游超级联赛
